endorsements.quote: establish internal periodic reviews of GenAI outputs and clinician interactions
establish error reporting processes for manufacturers and users (clinicians and patients), with respect to accuracy, safety and boundness of outcomes
create training programs to educate users about the limitations and functionalities of generative GenAI tools, in balancing the demand for efficiency with patient safety

As the impact of national regulations will depend upon, and evolve through, interpretation, application, guidelines, definitions, exceptions, and potential amendments, developers, administrators and clinicians should continuously assess their obligations and invest in compliance measures with national regulators, prior to the development, implementation and deployment phases.

determine the level of responsibility of the developers, the manufacturing company (e.g. with respect to the reported claims of the GenAI-enabled technology) and the deployers of the technology in a clinical environment
assess performance of subgroups, including by postal code; examine the application of the regulatory purview of claims by manufacturers

Instrument logging (prompts/contexts, seeds/decoding parameters, model version); require human sign-off for high-impact actions; track variance/instability signals; trigger monitor, detect, and correct, or rollback via PCCP if instability exceeds thresholds.
Run automated drift monitors; investigate alerts; apply threshold retuning or model/prompt updates under PCCP; document impact.
Measure adherence (override rates, near-miss reviews); refine workflows/training; tighten non-actionable categories if needed.
Pre-specify update triggers, locked tests, non-inferiority margins, and rollback criteria.

unlisted_practices: Establish a centralized reporting mechanism or registry for transparently reporting GenAI errors and monitoring performance.
Establish clear new definitions for errors and adverse events associated with GenAI outputs for monitoring and regulatory compliance.
Watermark GenAI-generated content to identify AI outputs and support continuous monitoring.
Establish local error adjudication boards to determine whether failures stem from product failure or GenAI algorithm implementation failure.
Establish a minimum audit-logging schema (inputs, prompts, decoding parameters, versioning) to support forensics and surveillance.
Use FDA-style market watch and safety alert paradigms to trigger recalls of GenAI-enabled devices.
Have GenAI models express uncertainty ("I have not seen this before" statements) to help clinicians and developers.
Engage diverse stakeholders, including patients, to understand the impact of GenAI devices on healthcare delivery.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/framework paper providing regulatory considerations and recommendations for generative AI-enabled medical devices across their total product lifecycle.
